messages:
leo: quick sync after the autoscale follow-up
we've got three candidate surfaces for reserved capacity: small per-tenant micro-reserves, a single global prewarm pool, or a layered approach with fast-local + slow-global.

karen: micro-reserves give predictable latency for top customers but blow up headroom when we have many midsize tenants. global pool is cheap but we lose isolation.

deepak: layered approach seems practical: each tenant gets a tiny local buffer (configurable) for <Xs bursts, global pool covers sustained spikes. operator enforces rates.

leo: agree. also leaning toward pushing sizing logic into the operator. CP should publish only "commit" (min) and "flex credits" numbers. operator translates flex credits -> local headroom.

ops-bot: alert: prewarm_pool_util=92% at 2026-02-12T09:12:43Z. consider spill routing.

karen: spill routing note: when global pool > 90% we should start steering non-SLA tenants to lower-cost model variants, not just reject. smoother UX.

deepak: design implications: operator needs three control decisions: admit (yes/no), borrow(via grace tokens), and reclaim. plus metrics stream: per-tenant local_util, borrow_amt, reclaim_events.

leo: proposed local config snippet for prototype:
```
reserve_policy:
  local_buffer_ms: 1500
  local_buffer_tokens: 5000
  decay_half_life: 60s
  borrow_charge_rate: 0.5 # tokens/sec billed to tenant when borrowing
  global_spill_threshold_pct: 90
```

karen: for billing/observability we must tag borrowed tokens separately and surface them in the console. ops needs an alert if borrow_rate spikes for a tenant.

deepak: edge case: noisy neighbor doing many microbursts will game decay. countermeasure: cap sustained borrow by EWMA of borrow_rate + short cool-down.

leo: can we keep CP simple: commit + max_allowed_borrow per tenant + global pool size. operator gets EWMA(util) and does the rest. keeps cross-team coupling small.

karen: tests: replay traces with mixed tenant shapes (heavy tail) + k8s operator PoC. verify fallback routing, billing tags, and circuit behavior when global pool depleted.

deepak: I'll hack the simulator and add a "malicious microburst" scenario. will log per-tenant borrow events. assigning myself.

leo: I'll draft the follow-up RFC and include rollout gate: start with internal-only tenants, then opt-in alpha for paying tenants, watch reservoir_util, borrow_charge.

karen: and include dashboards: per-tenant headroom, borrow_e2e_latency, model-variant spill counts.

ops-bot: note: rollout checklist created: rfc->sim->poC->smoke->canary.

leo: nice. short-term decision: prototype operator-driven layered reserves + CP publishes commit + borrow budget. next: spike schedule and owner list.
